name: HT9045 modal dialog bridge

transport.mailboxPattern: one request file plus one response file per channel
transport.fileWrite: write .tmp, flush and close, then atomically replace JSON and JSON/js shim
transport.ordering: seq must increase monotonically; requestId must be unique per invocation
transport.htmlRule: process only state=pending requests whose seq is newer than the last handled seq
transport.completionRule: C++ remains blocked until a matching state=completed response is received

displayEnvironment.rule: Do not design or validate phone/tablet layouts; this UI runs only on the fixed machine FullHD display.
displayEnvironment.zOrder: desktop windows < layout tools 9999 < #dialogBridge 20000 (Alert overlay) < #dialogAuth 21000 (login) < HTQwerty 99999 (keyboard); the Alert always covers every other page

showErrorMessage.returnMapping: response.selectedAction.code is returned unchanged as fNote->ReturnCode
showErrorMessage.pressedButton: BtnStart -> fNote::Start() (fMain->Start, SoftStart); BtnPause -> BtnPauseClick (SoftStop). null when closed by C++ close request.
showErrorMessage.zeroKCode: show an acknowledge button and return 0
showErrorMessage.closePolicy: When kCode is nonzero, browser X/Escape cannot complete the request; an enabled action is required.

showMyMessage.returnMapping: void; response confirms close reason and cleanup completion before C++ continues
showMyMessage.buttonMapping: OK when arguments.ok, runtime.secsGemAlarm, or runtime.haltHandler is true; otherwise Pause

dialogClose.responsibility: C++ detects and resolves IO; HTML only closes the targeted dialog and acknowledges completion.
dialogClose.normalResponseRule: HTML also writes the target Alarm/Message response so the blocking C++ function receives its action/result.

dialogAuth.producer: HTML login layer (verify) / C++ security check (result)
dialogAuth.trigger: request.auth.required==true and operator presses a closing action (Start/Pause/OK); ALARM_RESET never needs auth
dialogAuth.verifier: C++ only. HTML never compares passwords or access levels.
dialogAuth.resultRule: C++ writes state=completed with accepted true/false and the same authId; accepted -> HTML writes the normal response and closes; rejected -> dialog stays open, password cleared, operator may retry (palWrongPW).
dialogAuth.credentialsHandling: Plain credentials cross the local bridge only. Prefer WebView2/HTDialogHost.verifyAuth; in file mode C++ must read then immediately overwrite Dialog-auth-verify.json with state=consumed and must never log the password.
dialogAuth.closeRequestOverride: A C++ Dialog-close-request closes the dialog even while auth is pending (auth.bypassedByCloseRequest=true) because C++ already resolved the physical key.

alarmActionCodeRegistry._purpose: Authoritative list of the K_* bits that may appear in arguments.kCode, and which of them the alarm page can actually draw. 'alarmActionCodes' above is the flat name->value map, kept unchanged for backward compatibility; THIS block is what a producer must obey.

_verifiedAgainst.agreement: Identical in both trees: same 12 constants, same 9-entry button table, same dead set.
_verifiedAgainst.buttonTable: note.cpp:1244-1245 Ptr[] / KeyComp[] -- 9 entries. Same 9 repeated at note.cpp:2788, 2896, 3115, 3181, 3562, 3876.
_verifiedAgainst.visibilityRule: note.cpp:1537-1549  for(i=0;i<9;i++){ if(KeyCode & KeyComp[i]) Ptr[i]->Visible=true; else Ptr[i]->Visible=false; }
_verifiedAgainst.returnCode: note.cpp:3698  ReturnCode = KeyComp[i]  -- only for the button the operator selected
_verifiedAgainst.method: Every ShowErrorMessage() call site in both trees was parsed with a paren/quote-aware scanner and its kCode argument decomposed into bits. V912: 2000 sites (493 with kCode==0, 3 pass a variable). V899: 1763 sites (377 with kCode==0, 3 pass a variable).

roles.selectable: Present in note.cpp KeyComp[]. A set bit makes that button visible; selecting it and pressing START makes it the ReturnCode.
roles.retired: Constant still defined, but removed from Ptr[]/KeyComp[] and passed by no caller. Must never be set in kCode.
roles.panelOnly: Constant still defined but passed by no caller. The corresponding key is an independent panel button, not a kCode bit.

alarmButtonRule: For every SELECTABLE bit present in arguments.kCode, publish one button with that exact code and name. Bits whose role is not 'selectable' (FIX 0x0100, PAUSE 0x0400, START 0x0800) must never be set -- see kCodeGuard. BtnStart is visible iff kCode != 0; BtnPause is always visible; neither is a kCode bit.
failureRules: Never reuse an old response for a new request.
Never unblock ShowErrorMessage with an action code not enabled by kCode.
Do not close the HTML modal until response submission succeeds or the host explicitly cancels it.
A malformed request produces a correlated state=error response when requestId and seq are readable.
HTML must not read, poll, debounce, or interpret machine IO; C++ supplies trigger and resolvedAction.
A close request must match the active target requestId and requestSeq before HTML closes the dialog.
Dialog-close-response.json is emitted after the dialog is visually closed for both HTML actions and C++ close requests.
When request.auth.required is true, the normal response is written only after Dialog-auth-result accepted=true (or after a C++ close request).
The Alert overlay must stay above every other page; only the login layer and the keyboard may appear above it.

kCodeGuard._why: If kCode != 0 but carries no selectable bit, golden draws zero action buttons (note.cpp:1537-1549) while BtnStart is shown (kCode != 0). TfNote::Start() then walks its 9-slot Select[] loop, matches nothing, and skips the KeyCode==0 branch at note.cpp:3716 -- so START and PAUSE are both no-ops. The dialog can never be answered, the machine stays halted, and nothing is written to any log.
kCodeGuard.reachabilityEvidence: K_FIX, K_PAUSE and K_START have 0 call sites in both V912 and V899. The state is only reachable from a malformed producer-side request, not from golden control flow.
kCodeGuard.producerRule: A producer MUST NOT set FIX(256), PAUSE(1024) or START(2048) in kCode. Valid kCode is 0, or a bitwise OR of selectable values only (mask 0x02FF).
kCodeGuard.consumerRule: On receiving kCode != 0 with (kCode & 0x02FF) == 0, a consumer MUST treat it as a producer defect: log loudly and fall back to an acknowledge-only dialog (behave as if kCode == 0) so the operator can always dismiss the box. It MUST NOT render a dialog with no answerable control.
